features.name: first_person_plural_share
features.definition: What proportion of words across the counter-argument comments are first-person plural words (we, our, us)?
features.spec: import json,re; parse df['OC_comments'] as JSON list of strings; if missing/malformed return null; if list empty return null (no words). For all comments, tokenize with re.findall(r"[A-Za-z]+(?:'[A-Za-z]+)?", text.lower()) and count total words; count tokens equal to we, our, us, or starting with "we'" (we're, we'll, we've, we'd). Value = plural count / total words across all comments. Raw mechanical count; quotations and any outcome announcements in the text are not excluded.

h0: first_person_plural_share has no association with delta.
h1: Higher first_person_plural_share is associated with a higher probability of delta (OP view change).
note: Persuasiveness operationalized as the dataset outcome delta (OP changed view); association only. Language measured as share of words pooled over all available counter-argument comments (list order and per-comment outcomes unknown). Counts are raw text matches: quoted text (including quotes of OP) and possible outcome-related text within comments are not excluded, and 'ours/ourselves' are not counted since only we, our, us were named. Contractions with we' are counted as 'we'. Empty comment list gives null.
